Subject: Sundial billing units, rounding thresholds & discount framework

Hi Tara —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to surface a concise framing for how Redwood measures "billable units" (tokens + context aggregation) and to propose a simple discount framework that aligns with Sundial's expected usage profile. Quick summary up front:

- Billing unit: per-token generation + per-embedding units; we apply a context-window aggregation that groups short bursts within a 10-minute rolling window to a single billing unit.
- Minimums/rounding: we round up to 100-token buckets for per-call billing; for sustained sessions (>=30s) we amortize to 1,000-token buckets.
- Discount framework: tiered usage discount on net billable units (5% at 500k units/mo, 10% at 1.5M units/mo), plus a one-time pilot credit for transition months.

That said, you asked for concrete examples for how a short 280-token conversational exchange and a 12k-context summarize job would be billed and what concessions we can offer for the pilot month. I attached the usage sample you sent yesterday (sundial_usage_sample_q1.csv) and a short playbook that walks through the math.

Next steps: if you can confirm the two representative jobs (small chat vs. long-summary) are correct, I can follow up with Vanessa and Kimberly on exact invoice-line language and a pilot concession (we typically do a 25% first-month credit for first 90 days of contract start).

Best,
Michael

2) For long-summary jobs: our summarize job feeds a 12,000-token context and asks for a 600-token summary. Would the 12k context count fully against our billable units every run? If so, that scales linearly for us and would change how we approach batching.

3) Rounding: the 100-token bucket rounding — is that per-request or per-session after the 10-minute aggregation? Also can you share a simple invoice example (line items) showing the rounding?

Finally, procurement asked about a one-off concession for our proof-of-concept month: can you confirm whether the 25% first-month credit is applied as an invoice-level credit or as an offset to unit pricing in the billing system?

Tara — good questions. Answering inline and adding examples below. Vanessa/Kimberly — flagging to validate ops/invoice feasibility.

1) Prompt vs generated: We meter prompt + generated tokens (total tokens). Example: 40 prompt + 240 response = 280 billable tokens. This ensures deterministic billing regardless of tooling that trims prompts client-side.

2) Long-summary (12k context): We bill the full context tokens unless you use our prefix-KV caching or pre-tokenization/batching. Options:
   - Naive (no cache): each run bills 12,000 + 600 = 12,600 tokens.
   - With prefix caching and a shared artifact (recommended): if you reuse the same 12k context across multiple requests within a session, the KV cache charge applies once and subsequent runs bill only the generated tokens (600).

3) Rounding and aggregation: the 100-token rounding is applied after aggregation. So if multiple small calls aggregate into a single 10-minute window we sum the tokens and then apply the 100-token ceiling. Example invoice lines (simplified):
   - 2027-06-10 10:02 AM | 10-min aggregation | total tokens 348 -> billed as 400 tokens
   - 2027-06-10 10:35 AM | long-summary | total tokens 12,600 -> billed as 12,600 (no rounding beyond bucket)

Pilot credit: we apply pilot concession as an invoice-level credit (line item) — this keeps unit pricing stable for future true-ups. For the POC month we can do a 25% invoice credit cap up to $15k.

Attached is a short worked example using your sample file and three scenarios (naive, cached, batched). Let me know if you want me to push a mocked invoice into HubSpot for your procurement team to preview.

Best,
Michael

Looping internal ops and legal notes — short checklist before we commit to the pilot credit and the specific invoice language (copy suggestion below).

Checklist:
- Confirm KV caching applicability: product needs to confirm the 12k context is identical across runs; if not, mark as non-cacheable.
- Cap for pilot credit: approve $15,000 cap for 25% credit (SD-2027-087).
- Invoice language: we should show an itemized billing table with (a) billable tokens, (b) price per unit, (c) subtotal, (d) pilot credit line that references the signed MOU.
- Rounding documentation: we must include a short appendix (1 paragraph) explaining the 10-minute aggregation window and 100-token ceiling.

Proposed invoice credit line (verbatim):
"Pilot credit — 25% applied to invoice subtotal for proof-of-concept month, capped at $15,000, per MOU SD-2027-087."

Kimberly — can you confirm whether this wording is acceptable from finance/legal? If yes, Michael please send a preview invoice to Sundial procurement and I will sign off.
